claims.statement: Viewer3D caps Ember's orbit distance at 25 metres.

The active R4 Mid-Flank Fire Pilgrimage plan places the performer on a long contour ledge between a 100+ m upper volcanic edifice and a 60+ m fall to lower country; a high-source Flowy drainage passes west of the protected 4.5 m action radius and continues through the south scene boundary.

Reserved Gate 3/4 visual target, not an R4 measured-plan claim: blue-black basalt and rough obsidian dominate the frame; orange is confined to fissures and the banked, crusted river, with restrained mineral ochre as a secondary accent.

Historical surface research reserved for a future Gate 3/4 restart, not accepted R4 geometry: Fresh Rift uses young lava crust as Ember's surface base, exposes fractured basalt on scarps, shelters ash in depressions, and confines iron-rich alteration to lava-distance contact zones.

Mid-Flank Fire Pilgrimage R4 is the active geology direction: one continuous upper massif, one furnace saddle and high source, one contour-following performer ledge, one gravity-led Flowy drainage, one lower escarpment, and one explicit off-world downslope exit.
In the historical R1 benchmark, Flowy and MrLavaLoba2 produced 78.0 percent footprint intersection-over-union on the shared authored Ember DEM and benchmark parameters.

exemptions.name: walkability
exemptions.rationale: Ember is not a walkable museum room; performer action clearance and orbit sightlines are the relevant spatial checks.

exemptions.name: first-person-walk
exemptions.rationale: Viewer3D is evaluated by a default audience camera and complete registered orbit rather than first-person navigation; the fixed camera set and continuous orbit capture are the equivalent review proof.

exemptions.name: route-duration
exemptions.rationale: There is no authored player route in an orbit backdrop.

exemptions.name: sequence-parity
exemptions.rationale: This environment slice does not select or modify any TKA sequence.

exemptions.name: state-persistence
exemptions.rationale: Ember is a stateless Viewer3D environment. It introduces no room-owned interaction state to save or restore; performer and playback state remain owned by the shared viewer.

exemptions.name: typecheck
exemptions.rationale: The repository-wide check is baseline-red outside Ember. Gate 6 records all 455 errors and 29 warnings, confirms zero EmberScene or ObsidianPlatform diagnostics, and identifies the two Viewer3D diagnostics as the pre-existing Threlte layers typing mismatch rather than stage-sizing behavior.

regressions.reason: The adversarial review found that technical acceptance did not meet the approved gorgeous-scene art bar. Hero geometry, material separation, atmosphere, and all-angle composition require new registered 3D visual targets.

Gate 4 runtime review showed every performer facing backstage. The shared Viewer3D same-direction formation heading disagreed with its negative-Z audience camera, and cast changes restored the wrong heading.

The adversarial Gate 4 review found an organ-pipe silhouette, neon-zipper fissure, procedural horizontal texture bands, interface-like emissive lozenges, and weak rear-orbit coordination. Revision 4 keeps the same capability owner and rebuilds its art language around geological mass, negative space, occluded heat, and a complete coordinated orbit.
preserved: existing runtime asset and readiness owners

regressions.reason: R6 solved environmental continuity but still read as procedural graybox geology. R7 preserves that continuous spatial chassis and replaces the focal geological language with three audited Meshy multiview modules.
preserved: R6 continuous 380 by 335 m volcanic country

regressions.reason: R7 and the Blackglass atmosphere fixed focal geology and color separation, but the broad uniform basin and 23 m flat moat still made the stage read as a contained vignette. R8 compares three registered terrain topologies and advances the strongest world-scale composition.
preserved: four unique R7 Meshy geological landmarks

regressions.reason: R8 solved the terrain silhouette and shelf-to-world continuity, but one weathered-basalt texture triplet still skins the columnar hero and all three depth bands. R9 compares three camera-registered surface ecosystems and one director synthesis before changing the production material owner.
preserved: four unique R7 Meshy geological landmarks

regressions.reason: Austen rejected the accumulated environment as insufficiently realistic and required a bird's-eye, geology-first restart before further production iteration. The restart replaces motif-led terrain and spline-led lava with a measured plan, geological event sequence, and terrain-driven emplacement evidence.
preserved: Fresh Rift surface research and textures
Blackglass atmosphere, haze, plume, particle, and lighting systems
existing Meshy assets when they fit the new geological contacts
invalidated: previous Gate 3 registered visual target as a complete scene target
R10 production terrain and radial basin composition
seventeen-point Catmull-Rom ribbon as owner of the lava footprint

regressions.reason: The independent Gate 2 audit found that the approved R1 plan encoded a circular performance bowl, a smooth mound instead of an explicit collapse volume, a short simulator footprint that contradicted the authored continuation, south-up unlabeled plan evidence, stale clearance claims, and checkout-unstable manifest digests. Geometry and flow ownership therefore regress to Gate 1.1 before any new graybox.
preserved: one fissure source near runtime XZ (-72, 137)
existing Meshy assets and remaining credits
invalidated: R1 Gate 1 measurements and visual approval
R1 Gate 2 Blender source, GLB, manifest, renders, exemptions, and checks

regressions.reason: The R2 adversarial review found that the evidence overstated visual proof, the flow did not read causally from the registered runtime cameras, the quiet area still read as a circular stage, the collapse read as additive geometry instead of missing volume, the lava mesh modified simulator thickness, the GLB lacked runtime-recognized collision metadata, camera contracts were not exact, diagnostic nodes leaked into the review export, source and terminal semantics were ambiguous, and active documentation still pointed at invalidated later-gate work. Austen authorized a complete Gate 1.1 and Gate 2 correction with 'attack it!'.
preserved: Breached Rift Bench as the selected geological direction
Fresh Rift material research for a later gate
Blackglass atmosphere systems for a later gate
existing Meshy assets and unspent credits
invalidated: R2 Gate 1.1 plan approval and measurements
R2 lava-thickness transforms and false continuation semantics
R2 camera, collision, diagnostic-export, and portability claims
R2 Gate 2 Blender source, GLB, manifest, renders, and checks

regressions.reason: Austen rejected R3 because its technically valid broad-basin composition did not create the experience of standing halfway up a colossal volcanic flank, with consequential ascent above and descent below. R4 replaces the spatial target before any further Blender, runtime, material, or Meshy work.
preserved: Flowy ownership and pinned open-source geology pipeline
Fresh Rift material research for a later gate
Blackglass atmosphere systems for a later gate

checks.name: canon-conflicts
checks.evidence: Authority ledger records no story, performer, sequence, or adjacent-room mutation.

checks.name: source-digests
checks.evidence: The geology source ledger separates measured USGS data, scientific interpretation, production references, exact open-source pins and licenses, Meshy costs, and Ember-authored hypotheses.

checks.name: walkability
checks.evidence: Ember remains a Viewer3D orbit environment. The R4 report verifies low relief inside the protected 4.5 m action envelope while the contour ledge continues beyond the orbit; no material boundary encloses a circular stage.

checks.name: clearance
checks.evidence: The selected Flowy footprint preserves at least 2.500 m beyond the protected 4.5 m action envelope; the canonical R4 report owns the regenerated measurement.

checks.name: sightlines
checks.evidence: All eight exact-cap orbit samples clear the performer target; the eye sits 8.25 m above local ground, targets 1.75 m above it, and remains 25.000 m from target.

checks.name: final-view
checks.evidence: The north-up plan and true-scale section keep more than 100 m of upper mountain and more than 60 m of lower fall in one continuous section, while the exact opposite-side orbit proof tests both reads from the performer target.

checks.name: artifact-digest
checks.evidence: The canonical R4 Gate 1.1 report records SHA-256 digests for all review images and the checked-in little-endian float32 simulator raster.

approval.quote: Yeah that's better let's go with that

checks.name: artifact-digest
checks.evidence: The R4 graybox report records SHA-256 and byte length for every Blender, GLB, raster, still, motion, manifest, and source artifact.

checks.name: collision
checks.evidence: EMBER_Terrain is the sole visible collider and exports tka_camera_collision=true.

checks.name: route-duration
checks.evidence: The approved orbit-backdrop exemption is fulfilled by a 48-frame continuous exact-camera orbit plus eight registered 45-degree stills.

checks.name: sequence-parity
checks.evidence: The isolated R4 environment graybox does not select or modify a TKA sequence.
